pictures.scene: Frans Hals, Singing Boy with a Flute — the boy singing out with his mouth open and his eyes down on the music, a black cap with a great white plume pushed back off his hair, one hand holding the wooden flute across the open songbook and the other lifted beside him keeping the time, for the choirmaster to be accompanied by flutes, a Psalm of David
pictures.name: pd_hals_singing_boy_with_flute

pictures.scene: Nicolaes Maes, Old Woman Praying — the old woman at her table with her hands locked tight together over the open book, her lined face lifted and her lips parted, a white cap and a striped white collar against her plain black dress, the red cloth on the table with her spectacles and her pen laid down on it, give ear to my words O LORD, consider my groaning
pictures.name: pd_maes_an_old_woman_praying

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ enthroned in a pale blue robe inside a great blue oval ring of little winged heads, one hand raised in blessing and the gold rays going out behind Him over the whole field of gold, the ranks of haloed saints and angels standing and kneeling with their hands pressed together on either side, attend to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to You I pray
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Morning in the Riesengebirge — the first daylight coming up pale gold along the whole horizon with ridge behind ridge of blue mountains lying out under it and the mist still filling the valleys, the red rock of the summit catching the sun in front, and the little gold crucifix standing on the topmost crag with a tiny figure in white reaching back a hand to help another up to it, in the morning O LORD You hear my voice, at daybreak I lay my plea before You
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_morning_in_the_riesengebirge

pictures.scene: Carl Bloch, Girl at a Fisherman's Window — the girl standing outside the small panes in a white cap and a pink dress with a yellow apron, her finger lifted to tap on the glass and her eyes come straight in at us, the nets hanging down over the frame and the sea lying flat and bright behind her, and inside on the sill the glass of red and blue flowers and the day's fish laid out on the bench, and wait in expectation, for You are not a God who delights in wickedness
pictures.name: pd_bloch_girl_at_fishermans_window

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Tower of Babel — the huge tower going up tier on tier out of the rock, the finished white arcades below and the raw red brick above still open to the sky with scaffolding and cranes standing on it, ant-sized workmen all over the ramps and the stairways, and down in the front corner the stonecutters at work on the blocks in the grass, no evil can dwell with You, the boastful cannot stand in Your presence
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Cardsharps — the young player in black velvet and a lace collar bent over his hand with his eyes down on the cards, not seeing the older man in the striped sleeves leaning in right over his shoulder to read them, one gloved hand already signalling across the table where the dice and the backgammon board lie on the red carpet, You hate all workers of iniquity, You destroy those who tell lies
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_cardsharps

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Kiss of Judas — Judas wrapping his great yellow cloak right around Christ and leaning in with his face up to kiss Him, Christ standing still inside it with the gold halo behind His head and His eyes level on the man, the armed crowd pressed in all around them with clubs and torches and a drawn sword standing up against the blue sky, the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit, but I will enter Your house
pictures.name: pd_giotto_the_kiss_of_judas

pictures.scene: Emanuel de Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — the whitewashed stone arches going up and up into the light, the tall leaded windows standing all down the wall and the brass chandelier hanging in the middle of them, the preacher up in the high pulpit with his hand out over the people, the congregation in their black cloaks and white collars sitting and standing below him, a small child in a yellow jacket and a dog waiting in the sunlight on the floor, by the abundance of Your loving devotion, in reverence I will bow down
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk_amsterdam_during_a_sermon

pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole city lying out along the far ridge in the evening light behind its long wall, the great dome standing up gold and green in the middle of it, the Kidron valley dropping away in shadow with the olive trees scattered over it, and two or three travellers with their camels stopped on the stony track in front, looking across at it, toward Your holy temple, lead me O LORD in Your righteousness
pictures.name: pd_church_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Meindert Hobbema, The Avenue at Middelharnis — the straight rutted road running dead ahead to the village under a high pale sky, the tall bare-stemmed trees standing in a double line all down it with their small heads of leaves up at the top, the flat fields and the ditches on either hand, the church tower off at the left, and one man with his gun and his dog walking up the middle of the road toward the houses, because of my enemies, make straight Your way before me
pictures.name: pd_hobbema_the_avenue_at_middelharnis

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis — the one-eyed chief sitting at the head of the long lit table in a high gold crown, holding his great sword out flat across it, and the sworn men leaning in from both sides to lay their own blades against his and seal the oath, one of them with his back to us in a red coat and another holding up a dish, the whole room sunk in brown dark behind them, for not a word they speak can be trusted, destruction lies within them
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_conspiracy_of_claudius_civilis

pictures.scene: Gustave Courbet, A Burial at Ornans — the whole village standing out on the bare hillside at the graveside, the tall black crucifix held up over them against a grey sky, the priest reading from his book and the beadles in their red caps beside him, the bearers in white copes with the black crossed bones on them, and two boys in white standing in front with the holy water bucket, one of them turning his face up to the cross, their throats are open graves, their tongues practice deceit
pictures.name: pd_courbet_a_burial_at_ornans

pictures.scene: John Martin, Belshazzar's Feast — the vast palace courtyard of Babylon with its columns and terraces going back under a black sky, the ziggurat standing out pale in the smoke behind, and down in the front the long banquet table with the gold cups and dishes on it, the whole feast broken up around it, the prophet standing alone in his dark robe with his arm thrown out and the guests shrinking back and flinging up their hands, declare them guilty O God, let them fall by their own devices
pictures.name: pd_john_martin_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Joachim Patinir, Landscape with the Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — the whole sky burning red over the plain and the fire running along the two cities on the far bank, their towers and roofs black against it and the smoke going straight up, the river lying still and empty in between, the dark fields and the one pale standing pillar of salt on the near side, drive them out for their many transgressions, for they have rebelled against You
pictures.name: pd_patinir_sodom_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Peasant Dance — the villagers dancing out in the open at the church feast, the man in the black cap and the woman in the white headcloth and yellow apron come swinging past us with their feet off the ground, another couple spinning with their hands locked high behind them, the thatched houses and the church tower standing over the green and the whole village out on it, but let all who take refuge in You rejoice, let them ever shout for joy
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_peasant_dance

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Sheepfold by Moonlight — the flock packed close together inside the hurdle fence out on the dark plain, their backs catching the last of the light, the low wooden rails running right across the picture to shut them in, and the big pale moon standing just over the flat horizon in a quiet grey sky, may You shelter them, that those who love Your name may rejoice in You
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sheepfold_moonlight

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb — the Almighty enthroned above in a great red mantle with the triple crown and His hand raised in blessing, Mary reading at His right and John the Baptist at His left in his green robe, and below them the green meadow with the white Lamb standing on the altar and the blood running into the cup, the angels kneeling close around it, the dove blazing in the sky over it, and the crowds of prophets and apostles and martyrs and virgins coming in from every side to the fountain, for surely You O LORD bless the righteous, You surround them with the shield of Your favor
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_adoration_of_the_mystic_lamb

lines.text: For the choirmaster, to be accompanied by flutes.
A Psalm of David.
Give ear to my words, O LORD;
consider my groaning.
Attend to the sound of my cry,
my King and my God, for to You I pray.
In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice;
at daybreak I lay my plea before You
and wait in expectation.
For You are not a God who delights in wickedness;
no evil can dwell with You.
The boastful cannot stand in Your presence;
You hate all workers of iniquity.
You destroy those who tell lies;
the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I will enter Your house
by the abundance of Your loving devotion;
in reverence I will bow down
toward Your holy temple.
Lead me, O LORD, in Your righteousness
because of my enemies;
make straight Your way before me.
For not a word they speak can be trusted;
destruction lies within them.
Their throats are open graves;
their tongues practice deceit.
Declare them guilty, O God;
let them fall by their own devices.
Drive them out for their many transgressions,
for they have rebelled against You.
But let all who take refuge in You rejoice;
let them ever shout for joy.
May You shelter them,
that those who love Your name may rejoice in You.
For surely You, O LORD, bless the righteous;
You surround them with the shield of Your favor.
